meta.date: ~600 BC (in vision, from the valley of Lemuel)

world_behind.title: The whore was Israel's own idiom
world_behind.text: Long before John's Revelation, the prophets pictured covenant unfaithfulness as prostitution, loyalty sold for gain (Hosea's whole marriage; Ezek. 16). The vision's "whore of all the earth" (v. 11) speaks that inherited language at world scale: not sexual insult but covenant treason, monetized.

cites.quote: whore of all the earth

spans.text: whore of all the earth

world_behind.title: Two seers, one commission
world_behind.text: Nephi watches a man in a white robe who will "write the remainder of these things" (v. 21), and John's own book opens with exactly that assignment, to write the things which shall be hereafter (Rev. 1:19). The chapter shows the Revelation of John from the far side, six centuries before Patmos.

cites.quote: write the remainder of these things

spans.text: write the remainder of these things

world_behind.title: Sealed books were a known category
world_behind.text: Daniel was told to shut up his words and seal the book to the time of the end (Dan. 12:4), and John would later be told to seal the seven thunders (Rev. 10:4). Verse 26's writings "sealed up to come forth in their purity" (v. 26) belong to that tradition: a library already written, waiting on God's calendar.

cites.quote: sealed up to come forth in their purity

spans.text: sealed up to come forth in their purity

world_behind.title: Armor made of qualities
world_behind.text: Isaiah dressed the Lord in a breastplate of righteousness (Isa. 59:17), and Paul would issue the same equipment to the saints (Eph. 6:14). The vision's few, "armed with righteousness and with the power of God in great glory" (v. 14), fight in that armory; the record's battles are won wearing character, not steel.

cites.quote: armed with righteousness and with the power of God in great glory

spans.text: armed with righteousness and with the power of God in great glory

world_behind.title: Mother of abominations, mother of harlots
world_behind.text: The titles (v. 9, 16) match John's inscription on the woman's forehead (Rev. 17:5). Mother-language makes the institution generative: it breeds its kind. The vision's answer is also maternal: a covenant people being gathered, numbered, and blessed into a family.

world_behind.title: Pits were proverbs
world_behind.text: "that great pit, which hath been digged" (v. 3) returning on its diggers is wisdom-literature justice: he made a pit and digged it, and is fallen into the ditch which he made (Ps. 7:15–16). The vision runs the old proverb at the scale of hell itself.

cites.quote: that great pit, which hath been digged

spans.text: that great pit, which hath been digged

words.text: Belonging, in this chapter, is arithmetic: hearkening Gentiles "shall be numbered among the seed of thy father" (v. 2). To be numbered is to be counted in the census of a people — adoption recorded, not just felt, and the record will keep the verb for its most formal belongings and cuttings-off all the way down.

cites.quote: shall be numbered among the seed of thy father

spans.text: shall be numbered among the seed of thy father

words.text: Dug by the church of the devil for the saints, and filled by its diggers: "that he might lead away the souls of men down to hell" (v. 3). The vision's justice has a shape older than the vision (the trap returns on the trapper) and verse 4 files it under both headings at once: the devil's captivity, and the justice of God.

cites.quote: that he might lead away the souls of men down to hell

spans.text: that he might lead away the souls of men down to hell

words.text: The whore "had dominion over all the earth" (v. 11): rule that sits on top. Three verses later the Lamb's power "descended upon the saints" (v. 14): strength that comes down into. The two prepositions are the chapter's whole contrast between the kingdoms: one dominates from above, the other indwells.

cites.quote: had dominion over all the earth

spans.text: had dominion over all the earth

cites.quote: descended upon the saints

spans.text: descended upon the saints

words.text: "I, Nephi, am forbidden that I should write" (v. 28): the seer under orders about his own pen. The word marks the record's discipline: what it contains was commanded, and what it lacks was also commanded. Silence, here, is obedience wearing its work clothes.

cites.quote: I, Nephi, am forbidden that I should write

spans.text: I, Nephi, am forbidden that I should write

phrases.term: the taking away of their stumbling blocks
phrases.text: Chapter 13 diagnosed the Gentile injury (plain things taken, readers stumbling); this phrase is the cure's name. The Lamb manifests "in word, and also in power" (v. 1) precisely to remove what was placed in the road. The two chapters together are wound and treatment, and the record understands itself as part of the treatment.

cites.quote: in word, and also in power

spans.text: in word, and also in power

phrases.term: a great and a marvelous work
phrases.text: Isaiah's promised marvel (Isa. 29:14), quoted into an either/or: "either to the convincing of them unto peace and life eternal" (v. 7), or to their hardening. The work is one; its outcomes are two: the same manifestation that gathers some, condemns others by their response. Marvelous, in this record, is never automatically safe.

cites.quote: either to the convincing of them unto peace and life eternal

spans.text: either to the convincing of them unto peace and life eternal

phrases.text: The vision's great simplification: every allegiance on earth resolves into the church of the Lamb or "the church of the devil" (v. 10). Membership is determined by whom one belongs to, not where one's name is written, which makes the taxonomy useless for judging neighbors and piercing for judging oneself.

cites.quote: the church of the devil

spans.text: the church of the devil

phrases.term: the whore of all the earth
phrases.text: Covenant unfaithfulness at global scale, seated on the many waters of chapter 13; the ocean-highways become her throne. The image's force is economic: loyalty for sale. What the record sets against her is not a rival empire but a scattered family under covenant.

phrases.term: armed with righteousness and with the power of God
phrases.text: The record's most quoted armament, issued to a church whose "numbers were few" (v. 12). The list is deliberate: character first, power second, glory third, and no further weapon of numbers, wealth, or dominion. The saints win the vision's last war wearing what they are.

cites.quote: numbers were few

spans.text: numbers were few

phrases.text: The vision's closing formula, sealed with the record's honesty: "if all the things which I saw are not written, the things which I have written are true" (v. 30). True-though-partial is the record's standing claim about itself, and the Amen (the sign-off treated at 1 Ne. 9:6) locks the whole vision under oath.

cites.quote: if all the things which I saw are not written, the things which I have written are true

spans.text: if all the things which I saw are not written, the things which I have written are true

verses.label: v. 1–4
verses.title: The Gentile either/or
verses.text: Every clause is conditional: if they hearken, numbered, blessed, no more confounded; if they harden, the pit. The Gentile future (the reader's future, for most readers) is written entirely in if-grammar, and the pit waits for its own diggers, "according to the justice of God" (v. 4).

cites.quote: according to the justice of God

spans.text: according to the justice of God

verses.label: v. 5–7
verses.title: Mercy first, then the wo
verses.text: The angel's order of business is deliberate: confirmation that repentant Gentiles "shall be well with them" (v. 5) — stated as settled — before the wo of verse 6 is pronounced. Warning, in this record, always arrives with the escape route already on the table, and the marvelous work is announced only after both doors stand visibly open.

cites.quote: shall be well with them

spans.text: shall be well with them

verses.label: v. 8–10
verses.title: A question, then the taxonomy
verses.text: Before the two-church doctrine, a memory check: "Rememberest thou the covenants of the Father unto the house of Israel" (v. 8) Nephi's yes unlocks the rest. The order matters: the binary of verse 10 is safe only in a mind holding covenants, where it reads as God's faithfulness, not tribal license.

cites.quote: Rememberest thou the covenants of the Father unto the house of Israel

spans.text: Rememberest thou the covenants of the Father unto the house of Israel

verses.label: v. 11–14
verses.title: The whore and the few
verses.text: Dominion over all the earth on one side; on the other, saints "scattered upon all the face of the earth" (v. 14), few, and armed with qualities. The vision refuses to let the saints' safety rest on scale; the entire defense budget of the church of the Lamb is righteousness, power, and glory.

cites.quote: scattered upon all the face of the earth

spans.text: scattered upon all the face of the earth

verses.label: v. 15–17
verses.title: Wrath among the mother's nations
verses.text: Wars and rumors break out inside the dominion itself, and the angel marks the timing: when the wrath falls, then "the work of the Father shall commence" (v. 17) in fulfilling the covenants. The world's convulsions, in this vision, are the covenant calendar turning a page.

cites.quote: the work of the Father shall commence

spans.text: the work of the Father shall commence

verses.label: v. 18–27
verses.title: John, foreseen from behind
verses.text: A man in a white robe; the commission to write the remainder; the promise that his book, now wounded in transit (ch. 13), went forth pure from its source. Nephi is ordered off the topic, "thou shalt not write" (v. 25), and told others have written, sealed, and waiting. Prophecy here is a coordinated library, each seer assigned his shelf.

cites.quote: thou shalt not write

spans.text: thou shalt not write

verses.label: v. 28–30
verses.title: The seal on the vision
verses.text: Forbidden the remainder, Nephi closes with a witness formula three layers deep: he saw what his father saw, an angel confirmed it, and "the things which I have written are true" (v. 30). The vision that began with a desire to see ends with a signature under oath.

cites.quote: the things which I have written are true

spans.text: the things which I have written are true

chapter.title: Prophecy in the second person
chapter.text: The Gentile conditionals of verses 1–7 address the very population that would one day read the record — most readers meet themselves in this chapter's if-clauses. The vision's last panel is less prediction than summons, and the record knows exactly who is holding it.

chapter.title: The two-church doctrine, held safely
chapter.text: The binary arrives only after a covenant-memory check (v. 8), is defined by allegiance rather than roster, and is aimed at self-examination. The record's own descendants will be judged by it as surely as any Gentile institution — the taxonomy spares no one, including its keepers.

chapter.title: Power that descends versus rule that sits
chapter.text: The chapter's contest is drawn in prepositions: dominion over, power upon. Few-but-armed against many-and-seated is the vision's final geometry, and the record's entire doctrine of how God's people survive is packed into the direction the power moves.

chapter.title: A coordinated library of witnesses
chapter.text: Nephi writes his part, John will write the remainder, others have written and been sealed. The record presents prophecy as assigned labor across centuries and hemispheres, and presents itself, without embarrassment, as one shelf in a larger providence of books.

chapter.title: The vision ends in discipline
chapter.text: The seer is forbidden, consents, and certifies the fragment: true though partial. The close teaches the record's way of knowing in miniature (full confidence inside declared limits), the same balance Nephi struck at the vision's start (1 Ne. 11:17).

chapter.title: Down the mountain next
chapter.text: The cycle's four panels are complete: Messiah, the seed, the Gentiles and their books, the end of the world assigned to John. Chapter 15 opens back in the tent, where the men who could have asked for all of this are disputing about what it might mean. The unit's architecture makes its argument by descent.

applications.title: Read the if-clauses as addressed mail
applications.text: The Gentile conditionals include most modern readers by name. Read verses 1–2 once substituting "I" for "the Gentiles," and let the two verbs — hearken, harden — name this week's actual choice in one specific matter you have been stalling.

applications.title: Run the allegiance audit, inward only
applications.text: The two-church binary is a mirror, not binoculars. Take one ordinary day and sort its hours: which belonged, by allegiance, to the Lamb, and resist entirely the urge to run the audit on anyone else.

applications.title: Stock the issued armory
applications.text: The saints' equipment is righteousness, God's power, and glory, nothing that requires numbers or budget. Choose the piece currently thinnest in your kit and drill it deliberately this month: a righteousness repaired, a power sought by fasting, a glory given back in testimony.

applications.title: Stay on your shelf
applications.text: Nephi was forbidden John's assignment and took it well. Notice where you are straining to write what is not yours — another's calling, another's timetable, doctrine beyond what is revealed — and put the energy into the part that is assigned to you.

applications.title: Certify the fragment
applications.text: You cannot record everything God has done for you; you can certify what you have recorded. Close your journal entries and testimonies the way the vision closes, partial and true, and let the honesty carry more weight than completeness would have.

questions.text: Which stumbling block has the Lamb already taken out of my road, and have I ever named it in thanks?
Where am I currently hardening, not deciding against the Lamb, just letting a surface set?
If membership is by allegiance, whose church did my time, money, and attention belong to this week?
When the faithful few look small to me, what does this chapter say their actual strength is, and do I believe it?
What am I trying to author that was never assigned to me, and what assigned thing is waiting while I do?
Could I write "the things which I have written are true" under my own record of God's dealings, and if not, which is lacking: the writing, or the care in it?
